messages:
ana_support: Hi team — customer @ben reported 401s after they changed their infra. They moved traffic from an ALB/HTTP path to a GCP TCP NLB in front of an internal HAProxy, which then forwards to our Dedicated ingress in their VPC. Direct calls to Redwood succeed, but requests that traverse their stack are rejected with a scope/claim error.

ben_customer: Repro steps: 1) curl to https://internal-proxy.mycorp.local/api -> 401; 2) curl directly to https://redwood-dedicated.mycorp.internal with same Authorization header -> 200. Error payload we see: "{\"error\":\"invalid_scope\",\"details\":\"missing_permission:claims.user_email\"}". Token is an opaque SSO token issued by their IdP.

ana_support: They pasted the upstream request headers (sanitized):
```
Authorization: Bearer <opaque-token>
Host: redwood-dedicated.mycorp.internal
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.34
X-Forwarded-Proto: https
Cookie: session=...
X-Original-URI: /v1/generate
```
But our logs show the request arriving without any idp/assertion headers we normally use to map scopes to user claims (we expect x-sso-assertion or jwt_claims headers from their ext-auth).

sre_mike: Can you paste the Dedicated ingress ext_authz logs? If the proxy strips or re-encodes the Authorization header, our ext-authz step could fail to decode the token and fall back to scope validation that requires the email claim.

ben_customer: Logs from our side (haproxy) show it passes Authorization through, but we also run a small envoy-based ext-auth service that reads the opaque token, exchanges it for claims, then adds X-SSO-CLAIMS header. After switching to TCP NLB we had to re-enable proxy-protocol on HAProxy; our quick check shows the X-SSO-CLAIMS header is present on HAProxy->envoy but not on connections from HAProxy->redwood.

eng_infra_karim: Two likely failure modes here: 1) HAProxy configured to drop custom headers when using HTTP/1.0 or when doing PROXY protocol TCP passthrough; 2) Our Dedicated frontdoor expects the ext-auth downstream to set a specific header name (case-sensitive in some proxies) like X-Redwood-User-Claims. If HAProxy rewrites header capitalization or uses header folding, Istio/envoy on the Redwoods side might ignore it.

eng_platform_julie: Also check that HAProxy isn't converting the request to HTTP/1.0 which can cause header merging/truncation. Ben — can you share a tcpdump showing the raw request bytes hitting our ingress IP? Even a small pcap of the first 2 packets is useful.

ben_customer: Uploading snippet — tcpdump shows the Authorization header bytes intact, but the X-SSO-CLAIMS header is missing on the SYN->ACK stream we sent to redwood. It exists on HAProxy->envoy upstream. So it looks like HAProxy is not forwarding custom headers when proxy-protocol is enabled on that backend.

ana_support: For a repro I asked them to run a curl to their HAProxy endpoint with verbose flags:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <opaque-token>" -H "X-SSO-CLAIMS: user_email=ben@mycorp.com;roles=admin" https://internal-proxy.mycorp.local/v1/health
```
Response from HAProxy->redwood path: 401 invalid_scope. Response from direct to redwood: 200.

sre_mike: Workaround idea: Have HAProxy insert the claim into the Authorization header using a signed assertion (not ideal), or configure the HAProxy backend to use HTTP mode (not TCP) so it preserves headers. Also check for `http-request del-header` rules that may be conditional on proxy-protocol.

eng_infra_karim: Config snippet to watch for in HAProxy: `option forwardfor`, `send-proxy-v2`, and any `http-request set-header` rules. When `mode tcp` + `send-proxy` is used, HAProxy will not parse HTTP headers and will pass raw bytes, which can cause the ext-auth path (which expects to see headers added by the HAProxy HTTP layer) to be bypassed.

eng_platform_julie: On the Redwood side we can be tolerant: add a fallback that treats an existing Authorization header as authoritative even if X-SSO-CLAIMS missing (if token introspection returns required scopes). But that requires an opt-in config per customer for security. I'll open an internal feature request.

ben_customer: For now we flipped HAProxy to HTTP mode on the internal LB and the 401s stopped. Looks like a config mismatch. We'll keep HTTP mode until we can validate proxy-protocol semantics. Thanks for the fast triage. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: infra-change: HAProxy backend toggled to http mode by @ben at 2026-03-17T15:02:03Z

ana_support: Closing loop — root cause: HAProxy TCP/proxy-protocol path bypassed header-insertion ext-auth flow, removing SSO claim header our Dedicated ingress relies on for permission checks. Recommend adding a short KB entry and a checklist for customers moving to TCP NLB: ensure header-preserving backend mode or opt into Redwood token-introspection fallback.

sre_mike: I'll add a small runbook entry with the specific HAProxy config lines to avoid (and a sample `http-request set-header X-SSO-CLAIMS` snippet).

eng_infra_karim: Filed GH issue: infra/proxy-interop#432 — propose adding a detection metric when ext-auth headers are missing but Authorization present.

ana_support: Marking internal ticket as resolved; customer confirmed fix.
